context: Crime drama scene. A detective warns a suspect who is being confrontational.
intended_meaning: You are taking increasingly dangerous risks and are being warned to stop.
acceptable_alternatives: تۆ یاری بە بەختی خۆت دەکەیت.
notes: Idiomatic expression warning against escalating risk.

context: Family drama. An elder reprimands a young family member for disrespectful speech.
intended_meaning: Stop talking immediately and do not say such disrespectful things.

context: Backstage before a theater performance.
intended_meaning: Good luck on your performance.
notes: Classic theatrical idiom meaning good luck.

source: I am in over my head.
context: Suspense thriller. Protagonist realizes a conspiracy is far larger than anticipated.
intended_meaning: I am involved in a situation that is far too difficult for me to handle.
gold_sorani: من لە سەرتاپای ئەم بابەتەدا نوقم بووم.
acceptable_alternatives: ئەم بابەتە لە توانای من بەدەرە.
تێوەگلاوم لە کارێک کە لە من بەدەرە.

context: Action conflict. Father refuses to allow villain to take his children.
intended_meaning: I will never permit this to happen under any circumstances.

context: Romantic comedy. Character looks out the window during a dramatic downpour.
intended_meaning: It is raining very heavily.

source: You stabbed me in the back!
context: Corporate thriller. CEO confronts a partner who secretly sold their shares.
intended_meaning: You betrayed me when I trusted you.
notes: Betrayal idiom — must not be translated literally as stabbing.

context: Adventure film. Team leader stops an impatient member from charging ahead.
intended_meaning: Wait, be patient, slow down.

source: Don't let the cat out of the bag.
context: Spy thriller. Handler instructs agent not to reveal classified info.
intended_meaning: Do not reveal the secret.

source: I have bigger fish to fry.
context: Police procedural. Detective dismisses a minor case to focus on a major investigation.
intended_meaning: I have more important things to deal with.
gold_sorani: کاری گرنگتر لەمە هەیە بۆ ئەنجامدان.

context: Legal drama. Lawyer tells client they must appear in court despite the risks.
intended_meaning: It is time to accept responsibility and deal with the consequences.
gold_sorani: کاتی ئەوەیە بەرگریت بکەیت و ئەنجامەکە قبوڵ بکەیت.
unacceptable_literal_examples: کاتی ئەوەیە گوێ لە موسیقا بگریت.

context: Sitcom. Friends are talking about someone who suddenly walks in.
intended_meaning: The person we were just talking about has arrived.

source: The ball is in your court.
context: Negotiation scene. Business rival delivers final offer and waits for response.
intended_meaning: It is now your decision to make.

context: Dark comedy. Character casually reports the death of a disliked neighbor.
intended_meaning: He died.
notes: Death euphemism. Must be idiomatic, not literal.

context: War film. Sergeant warns soldiers to stay alert during a patrol.
intended_meaning: Stay very alert and watch carefully.
gold_sorani: ئاگادار بن و باش سەیر بکەن.

source: Hit the nail on the head.
context: Investigation scene. Detective identifies the exact motive behind the crime.
intended_meaning: Described something with exact precision and correctness.

context: Drama. Main character declines a dinner invitation.
intended_meaning: Feeling slightly ill or unwell.

context: Comedy mystery. Friends demand a confession from someone keeping a secret.
intended_meaning: Tell the truth or reveal the secret now.

source: You're barking up the wrong tree.
context: Thriller. Interrogated suspect warns detective they suspect the wrong person.
intended_meaning: Following a completely mistaken line of thought or accusing the wrong person.
acceptable_alternatives: بە هەڵە گومانت لە من کردووە.

source: I had to burn the midnight oil.
context: Biopic. Researcher explains how they solved a difficult problem overnight.
intended_meaning: Worked late into the night.
